correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact Euler map and its unique positive invariant form for a fixed step. Brouwer fixed points on normalized positive semidefinite covariance cones yield positive-definite primal and dual eigenmatrices, since each elliptic update has no real eigenline. The determinant-root Minkowski inequality gives spectral radius at least one; strict equality forces a single step size. Positive dual eigenmatrix gives uniform two-sided exponential moment growth for every nonzero initial state, and operator domination proves this exponent is the spectral radius of the explicit moment matrix. Analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation gives the exact quadratic variance coefficient. Python exact fractions passed 107 independent algebra/path checks. Finite checks are not the proof of unbounded-horizon dynamics.

value.rationale: The natural and previously motivated stochastic time-stepping construction raises a real stability question: preserving symplecticity per random update need not preserve expected numerical energy indefinitely. The theorem answers it completely for the canonical harmonic oscillator, giving a sharp iff distributional boundary, a nontrivial positive-operator structural proof, exact moment recurrence and a predictive small-variance rate. It distinguishes all-iteration mean-square behavior from established conditional finite-horizon guarantees, without claiming stronger effects or external certification.
